📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If your soundbar just hasn't been making your movies sound as cinematic as they deserve, then perhaps it's time you entered the world of the home theater with one of the best AV receivers.

That's how you get the best surround experience possible, after all. If you're willing to invest in some speakers as well. One per channel, of course. We never said it would be cheap.

Our favorite amplifier at the moment is the Denon AVR-X4800H. It's an excellent performer with loads of great features, and doesn't cost as much as similar options. or if you need something that handle any format you throw at it, I'd recommend the Marantz Cinema 50.

Industry observers note that why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

In a recent development, A sonic tour de force, the X4800H is a home theater amplifier with long-term appeal. The provision of a full board of 8K/4K 120Hz HDMI inputs, and coverage of all the significant home cinema sound formats, ensures that this Denon amp will partner any display or source you might acquire for a long time to come.

It's not the smallest box, but that's because it's fill with loads of amplification tech, supporting nine channels for massive surround sound or an Atmos system. The screen on the front makes it easy to read what mode its in, and then there's an easy setup mode when you plug it into your TV or projector. From there, you can setup all of the different settings and features to get the most out of your receiver.

Recent findings suggest that the sound is powerful enough to make the experience feel almost physical. The soundstage is crisp and detailed, but there is a sense of power and precision as well; directional panning is totally convincing. While Denon rates on-board power at 9x 125W (into 8 Ohms) / 200W (into 6 Ohms), it sounds rather more muscular than that.

In a recent development, you'll get the most out of this amplifier while watching movies, especially those with detailed sound effects and soundtracks. But this also makes it a great companion for music, with your favorite tracks coming out of the two-channel stereo sounding light and agile, with immersive 3D audio mixes.

Industry observers note that the Marantz Cinema 50 is one of the most future-proof home theater amps we've seen. The connectivity on offer is truly impressive with 8K and 4K 120Hz support, 6 HDMI inputs plus three outputs, and an impressive auto calibration system.

Sources indicate that format support is extensive with Dolby Atmos, DTS:X and Auro 3D capable, as well as Sony’s 360 Reality Audio. It’s also IMAX Enhanced certified, which is a great advantage if you like to stream movies on Disney+, after the tech giant introduced IMAX audio mixes for select movies (including a lot of Marvel) in mid-2024.

If you’re looking for an AV amp that can deliver massive dynamics, with whip-crack fast transients and a fearsome bass extension, the Cinema 50 doesn’t disappoint. It’s a tremendously exciting listen and steers gunfire shootouts beautifully, with effortless panning, and even at high volume there's no hint of strain.

It does music well too. Marantz’s lauded HDAM amplification circuitry is warm and melodious. In 2-channel mode, we’d say the Cinema 50 is comparable to a high-quality mid-range stereo amp, and with strong format support is as future-proof as they come right now.

Sources indicate that the Marantz Cinema 70S is a half-height lifestyle AV receiver perfect for smaller spaces and viewing rooms. The sonic signature has a warm sound that works with hi-res audio as well as movies and gamers.

According to recent reports, you can run a 5.1.2 Atmos setup with a uniform 50W delivered across all 7 channels and it was peerless with movie soundtracks. In "Army of Thieves" (Dolby Atmos, Netflix), our reviewer really got the sense that they were travelling into the inner mechanism of the safe when Ludwig Dieter lays his hands on the lock, during the safecracking competition. The clicky travel of the dial is crisply delineated against the symphonic score, which rises all around.

Hooked up to a Fire TV stick listening to Dolby Atmos music mixes from Tidal, our reviewer was thrilled at just how seamlessly the 360 presentation was. Billy Porter’s "Break A Sweat" places the listener firmly in the middle of the dance floor, with horns in the surround, the vocal dead center and the main beat gyrating across the LCR.

In our 5.1.2 configuration, there were no sonic gaps or dips with any kind of content, just a totally immersive listening experience.

When testing models for inclusion in our best AV receivers page, we play a range of media, including movies, music and games, to evaluate overall sound quality performance.

We also test any companion software that may come with an AV receiver, and factor in how easy it is to set up and use each receiver with a reference speaker system. Other features we consider include the different kinds of connectivity options, all of which determine how well it will work with your home entertainment setup.

We also take into account power output, the number of supported audio channels and subwoofer outputs, and available processing software for decoding movie soundtracks as well as their ability to handle music sources — all factors that greatly affect how each speaker will sound in your living room.

An AV receiver is an amplifier that's designed for home cinema and movie watching. You plug it into your TV with an HDMI cable, and then it takes the audio signal, and processes it for separate speakers. You need to have speakers for an AV receiver to work — it's a kind of go-between device.

You could have as many speakers as you like, although there's a minimum of two. Everything from a normal stereo (two speakers) up to a much larger surround setup (7.1 and above). It needs to be plugged into the power as well. Remember to budget for speakers with an AV receiver.

This is a big question to ask yourself. Do you have the space for multiple speakers around the room? What kind of watching do you do? Can you budget for more than two speakers?

In a recent development, if the answer to any of those questions is no, then you don't need an AV receiver. I'd argue, in fact, that very few people need an AV receiver — you're much better off with the space-saving capabilities of one of the best soundbars, or the musical chops of a pair of HDMI-enabled powered speakers like the Kanto Ren.

But, if you love watching movies, you've got plenty of space, plenty of budget, and permission from your significant other, then an AV receiver might be just what you've been looking for.

According to recent reports, everyone's movie room is different. They're different shapes and have different furniture inside, which can affect the sound of your system. In order to make movies sound their best, no matter what's in your room, manufacturers have built room correction systems that listen to the sound and then compensate for the differences in decor and shape.

Some, like Denon and Yamaha, have made their own room correction systems built into companion apps. Many amplifiers come with microphones to aid the process, and its built into the setup of the device. It's well worth going through the stages, and it can make a major difference to bass extension and surround sound placement.

Yes, you can! And you most certainly should. Your AVR can be used as the central pillar of a home music system, especially as more and more devices can connect to whole-home music streaming devices. That means you can connect your turntable, CD player, or other devices.

It has been revealed that for turntables, there are a couple of things to bear in mind. Some AVRs do not have a built-in phono pre-amp, and so you'll need either a separate device or a TT with a pre-amp built in. If your AVR has a built-in pre-amp, you'll need to make sure you connect your TT to the correct RCA plugs. They'll be labeled "phono.".

It has been revealed that they are good for gaming, though it depends on the types of games you like to play. For immersive RPGs filled with movie-like cutscenes and massive set pieces, you're in for a sonic treat. For fast-paced online shooters, you'll likely want to stick with your gaming headset.

It has been revealed that just make sure that your latest AVR and your TV support HDMI 2.1 for the best audio and visual experience possible. That means that 4K120Hz will be supported, along with Variable refresh rates and other game-specific features can be supported.

Recent findings suggest that if you want to get the most out of the home theater experience, then you should pick up some Atmos speakers for the full effect. Without them, you won't get the spatial audio channels that make the sound come from above you — it's well worth it if you can stump up the cash.

Buying something as complex and multi-talented as an AV receiver can be overwhelming to a casual consumer, so if you’re serious about transforming your sound output into something more theater-like, start educating yourself on the necessities by familiarizing yourself with the things to consider.

Recent findings suggest that something to know right out of the gate is that most seven-channel AV receivers support a speaker configuration of 5.1.2, which is the standard 5.1 surround layout with two additional height/up-firing speakers. Models that feature nine channels of amplification can be used for either 5.1 with four Dolby height speakers (5.1.4) or 7.1 surround with two height channels (7.1.2). Speaker models such as those in the upcoming Klipsch Reference series could make a great partnership for a home cinema setup, and has several upward-firing height speakers to meet Dolby Amos requirements.

Sources indicate that finding the best AV receiver isn’t just about HDMI inputs. Sure we like plenty of inputs, but the number of outputs is crucial too, particularly if you initiative on running both a flatscreen and a projector in the same room.

If you're considering an AV receiver as a connectivity hub for a music system as well as movies, then be sure to check out our guide to the best turntables for any budget. Many of the receivers available today come with a built-in moving-magnet phono stage to enable vinyl playback from any of the record decks we've tested.

Resolution and frame rate support.

In a recent development, do you need 8K or High Frame Rate HDMIs? If your AV receiver is unlikely to have a games console connected then the answer is no. In which case there are some great deals to be had on AVRs with regular HDMI 2.0 inputs.

In a recent development, dolby Atmos compatibility is a given (and by default that means you’ll get DTS:X too), but how many channels do you need? Given the option, 9 channels always trump 7, because it opens up more speaker options such as 5.1.4 or 7.1.2, for example.

Don’t have a full Dolby Atmos home theater loudspeaker setup? Look for a model that offers height virtualization technology, so you can enjoy an immersive audio experience even when you don’t have a full set of physical speakers.

In a recent development, power isn’t just about roof-raising volume, and even if you’re not lucky enough to have a dedicated movie room, a model with massive amplification makes sense. A high power output means an AVR can deliver dynamic transients, and pressure load a space without clipping or strain.

Recent findings suggest that one of the most confusing things about any kind of home cinema system is the surround sound channel numbers you'll often spot on the box. What do they mean, and what do they tell you about the receiver that you're about to buy?

Industry observers note that those numbers denote the channels that are available to use with the receiver. It's broken up into three different sections. The first number is the surround channels. The middle is for subwoofers. The final number is the height channels, for Dolby Atmos and DTS:X.

Say, for example, that you've got a receiver that's got a 7.1.4 surround sound setup. That means you've got seven surround channels that you could use for a centre, left and right stereo, two side surrounds, and then a pair of rear surrounds. You've then got a single subwoofer channel.

Industry observers note that finally, you've got four height channels that you can place around the room in predetermined Atmos spots. You can use Atmos testing videos to make sure all your speakers are in the right place.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, anthropic has opened Skills over MCP in public beta, letting apps that connect to Claude ship playbooks alongside their tools. Tasks, for long background jobs, and Elicitation, which pauses for user input, are now generally available, with File Uploads coming soon.

Industry observers note that apps that plug into Claude through MCP can now also tell it how to use them, Anthropic said on Tuesday. The feature, Skills over MCP, is in public beta in Claude and Claude Code.

According to recent reports, MCP is the open standard Anthropic released two years ago to link AI agents to outside apps and data. Servers built on it already list the tools Claude can use. With skills, they can also ship step-by-step guides and best practices, which Claude loads only when needed.

Shopify uses skills to help Claude design and upgrade online stores, and HubSpot to onboard customers. Skills update with the server, so consumers have nothing extra to install. More apps are opening up, too: Canva opened its MCP server to all developers on Tuesday.

Recent findings suggest that the beta is on by default for Pro, Max and Ultra plans. Team admins can switch it on, and Enterprise support is coming soon.

Recent findings suggest that two other features are now generally available. Tasks lets a server run long jobs in the background while Claude keeps working, which ZoomInfo uses for deeper research. Elicitation lets a server pause and ask the user for input.

GitHub, for example, makes users type a repository’s name before an agent deletes it. Supabase confirms costs before creating a paid project. A fourth feature, File Uploads, will soon let Claude send PDFs, spreadsheets and images to servers.

It has been revealed that the features are part of MCP, so servers that support them also work in other compatible apps. Anthropic indicates MCP now sees over 700M SDK downloads a month. In August, OpenAI and four rivals agreed on a standard for packaging skills and MCP servers.

Skills carry risks, too. That same month, researchers found malicious agent skills that stole passwords and keys after about 1.7 million installs.

Will Siri AI threaten Apple’s environmental target, given Google and Meta admissions?

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1004 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, I think Apple can reasonably claim to be the leading tech giant when it comes to its environmental credentials.
  • All of this could potentially be put at risk by the company’s ambitions for Siri AI, however, as Meta joins Google in admitting it is now unlikely to meet its own 2030 net zero promise, thanks to the huge power demands of the data centers powering its AI services ….
  • Apple’s environmental record isn’t entirely perfect.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, I think Apple can reasonably claim to be the leading tech giant when it comes to its environmental credentials. It has led the way with its use of renewable energy, made significant strides with carbon-neutral production, and removed plastic from all its packaging.

All of this could potentially be put at risk by the company’s ambitions for Siri AI, however, as Meta joins Google in admitting it is now unlikely to meet its own 2030 net zero promise, thanks to the huge power demands of the data centers powering its AI services ….

Apple’s environmental record isn’t entirely perfect. For example, when it claimed that the Apple Watch Series 9 and Ultra 2 were carbon neutral back in 2023, that claim was described as “bogus,” with the EU banning Apple from repeating it. The manufacturer has also been criticized for pushing a relentless annual iPhone cycle, encouraging frequent upgrades.

Overall, however, Apple has first-rate credentials when it comes to the environment. It was way back in 2018 when the organization hit its goal of running its own operations off 100% renewable energy. This includes all Apple facilities, from Apple Park through data centers to its worldwide retail store network.

I said at the time that using more environmentally friendly packaging should be the company’s next priority, and it has indeed made great progress with this over the years, succeeding in removing all plastic packaging earlier this year.

Recent findings suggest that after its own operations, Apple set about trying to tackle the power usage of its manufacturing partners. Back in 2020, the tech giant set a goal of having its entire supply chain be carbon neutral by 2030. Just four years later, Apple said it was 95% of the way there.

The tech giant also helps fund and support a wide range of environmental initiatives around the world. Just a few examples include conservation in China’s national parks, environmental protection and carbon removal in Australia and New Zealand, and helping to fund the build-out of renewable energy capacity in India.

Industry observers note that potentially, however, the vast energy demands of the data centers powering AI services could put its 2030 goal at risk. Other tech giants have already admitted that it may lead them to fail to hit their own renewable energy promises.

Back in 2024, for example, Google CEO Sundar Pichai mentioned that the AI boom was “challenging” to the tech giant’s 2030 carbon-free goal. CNET reports that Meta is now also admitting that it may fail to hit the same target.

Meta’s data center and sustainability chiefs wrote that the organization is “re-evaluating our timelines, sequencing, and interim milestones — including the 2030 timeframe for our net zero emissions goal and our near-term intensity targets.” In an emailed statement to CNET, a Meta spokesperson added, “We remain committed to net zero, but are re-evaluating the 2030 timeline.”.

Notably, a lot of Siri’s most advanced AI capabilities are right now powered by Google’s Gemini models.

At the same 2024 event where Google expressed doubts, Apple reiterated its commitment to its 2030 target. Then-CEO Tim Cook repeated this assurance later the same year, although admitted it would be challenging.

More challenges, yes. But are we coming off the goal? No, definitely not. With more data centers, you use more renewable energy, and we’ve built that muscle now […] I feel very good about 2030.

In the company’s most recent environmental progress report, it said that it was was still using 100% renewable energy despite using over 2.5 billion kWh of electricity to power its data centers.

Industry observers note that we’re proud that 100 percent of that electricity came from renewable sources including solar, wind, and low-impact hydropower. To cover our needs, we build our own renewable power projects and work with utilities to purchase clean energy from locally obtained resources. We’re staying at 100 percent even as Apple’s data center capacity continues to grow.

The same report stated the company had achieved zero water use for cooling at its latest data centers.

At our three newest data centers, we use high-efficiency air-cooled chillers instead of water-cooled systems, resulting in zero water use for cooling.

Industry observers note that however, the greatest challenge for Apple lies ahead. The reason that Google and Meta are now backtracking on their promises is that both companies now have massive AI capabilities. As yet, Apple does not.

It has been revealed that what happens as Apple expands Siri AI capabilities as usage increases, and as the firm moves into agentic AI features? Is it realistic for the company to maintain its 100% track record with vastly greater data center energy usage?

Greenpeace expressed its own doubts earlier this year.

According to recent reports, “AI will be the defining test of Apple’s climate commitments,” spokesperson Avex Li states. “To preserve Tim Cook’s environmental legacy, the company will need to show that AI growth can be accommodated within its existing climate commitments through absolute emissions reductions, additional renewable energy investment, and longer-lasting products.”.

Apple did not respond directly but merely pointed to its past statements and most recent environmental progress report.

I don’t doubt the company’s desire to maintain its track record, but if Apple does join the likes of Google and Meta in becoming a major AI player, sticking to its 2030 timing is going to become increasingly difficult.

According to recent reports, do you think Apple will succeed? Please share your thoughts in the comments.

According to recent reports, to help you find the best all-in-one printer, we put each model through an extensive range of printer tests, including timed prints of text, mixed text and graphics and color photos. The resulting prints are carefully examined for errors and issues, and compared with samples from other printers to determine the print quality.

We time every test print to see how rapidly the machine handles document printing, and closely examine the finished product to determine how well different printing tasks are handled.

We also test the scanning and copying functions of the printer, timing how rapidly it captures a page and comparing the results to the original images to determine how well it captures color and detail.

To measure the cost of owning and operating a printer, we look at the current street price of ink refills and the estimated number of pages that each cartridge can produce, and calculate the cost of printing a single page.

Sources indicate that not sure which all-in-one printer to buy? Obviously, you want a printer that performs well, so all of our reviews and rankings discuss a printer's output quality and speed, but there's more to an all-in-one printer than just how promptly it can crank out documents.

Sources indicate that some companies even offer subscription services that save you money while sending you ink just in time to replace that empty cartridge. Learn more in our article HP Instant Ink vs. Canon vs. Epson: Are ink subscriptions worth it?

Ink-tank printers, a type of Inkjet, usually offer the lowest running costs because their refill bottles deliver far more pages than conventional cartridges.

In our guide, the Brother INKvestment MFC-T780DW is the best-value option for home or light-office use, while the Epson EcoTank Pro ET-5850 pairs very low per-page costs with the capacity and features needed for heavier business printing.

You should compare current cost-per-page figures with your expected print volume, not just the printer’s upfront price.

Choose an inkjet if you print color graphics or photos, want a lower upfront price or value the low ongoing costs of an ink-tank model. Choose a laser all-in-one if your priority is fast, sharp text documents and a responsive office workflow.

The Canon Color imageCLASS MF753Cdw II is our top pick, as it's a fast laser workhorse, whereas the Canon MegaTank Pixma G3290 is the stronger fit for photo printing.

An automatic document feeder (ADF) is worthwhile if you regularly scan, copy or fax multi-page documents, as it feeds the sheets for you instead of requiring one page at a time on the scanner glass.

It matters less for occasional household printing or photo-focused use. Also check its capacity and whether it supports double-sided scanning: an ADF does not automatically mean both sides can be scanned in one pass.

It has been revealed that some can, but not every all-in-one printer with an ADF supports automatic double-sided scanning or copying. Do not confuse duplex printing with duplex scanning: a printer may print on both sides of a sheet while still requiring you to turn over originals when scanning or copying.

Check the model’s specifications before buying; the Brother INKvestment MFC-T780DW has an ADF but does not support duplex scanning or copying through it.

Industry observers note that many current all-in-one printers support wireless mobile printing through a manufacturer app, Apple AirPrint or another built-in service. The Canon MegaTank Pixma G3290, for example, supports Wi-Fi and printing through a smartphone app.

Before buying, confirm that the printer works with your phone or tablet, operating system, preferred app and network setup. Some features may require the device and printer to be on the same Wi-Fi network.

AirPods Pro 3 (now only $149, down from $249) offer many advantages over AirPods Pro 2, but after a year of use, the improvements to Active Noise Cancellation alone have proven worth the upgrade.

I’ve been using AirPods Pro 3 for over a year, and they had a lot to live up to because I already loved AirPods Pro 2 so much. Initially I found the new ear tips less comfortable, but thankfully that problem went away after a little extra time.

Some highlights of AirPods Pro 3 include the longer battery life, with 8 hours per charge compared to 6 on the previous model. The charging case’s new Ultra Wideband chip also makes it easier to find when it’s lost. Some customers will appreciate the heart rate sensor, but I wear an Apple Watch all the time so it doesn’t benefit me much.

These new features are nice to have, but Active Noise Cancellation is where AirPods Pro 3 become a major upgrade. Apple says it’s “the world’s best in-ear Active Noise Cancellation.” Here’s how the new ANC compares to previous models:.

I spend nearly my entire workday with AirPods Pro 3 in my ears. Whether I’m working from home with young kids around or at a busy coffee shop, I rely on ANC to block out background noise and help me focus.

One reason I’ve been especially impressed with the ANC upgrades is that I didn’t have any real complaints about ANC on AirPods Pro 2. But Apple managed to deliver improvements in AirPods Pro 3 I had no idea I needed, and when I’ve tried going back to AirPods Pro 2 I couldn’t believe how much noise was let in.

If Active Noise Cancellation is important to you, I highly recommend AirPods Pro 3.

Sources indicate that guodong Zhang, Zihang Dai and Manuel Kroiss, three of xAI’s co-founders, have launched Epochal, a startup building AI that forecasts events. Zhang has put in $100M of his own money, Bloomberg reported. Its first product, Time Portal, lets agents browse the web as it was at past dates, so they can practise forecasting without seeing the outcome.

It has been revealed that three of xAI’s co-founders have released Epochal, a startup that wants to teach AI to forecast events. Guodong Zhang, Zihang Dai and Manuel Kroiss confirmed the firm and its first product on Tuesday.

In a recent development, zhang has put in $100M of his own money, Bloomberg reported. No other investors have been named.

In a recent development, all of xAI’s co-founders have since left the company, as Elon Musk rebuilds it after its merger with SpaceX. Another co-founder, Igor Babuschkin, raised $1.1bn for his own startup, River AI, in August.

Today’s AI models learn from an internet where they can already see how things turned out, Epochal says. People, by contrast, have to make choices before they know the result.

Recent findings suggest that its first product, Time Portal, lets AI agents browse the web as it looked at any moment over the past 30 years. Epochal states it covers more than 1 trillion pages, down to the minute on busy sites. A matching Linux sandbox sets its clock, software and downloads to the same date, so agents cannot spot the trick.

To test it, Epochal ran forecasting agents on 347 live questions from prediction markets Kalshi and Polymarket. Weeks later, it replayed the same questions through Time Portal. In its own test, the replayed forecasts closely matched the originals, with a correlation of 0.98.

Recent findings suggest that developers can try a limited version for free. Epochal has not said how it gathered the archive or whether the pages are licensed.

Tired of Wi-Fi drops throughout your home? The best mesh Wi-Fi systems can eliminate internet dead zones and turn your house into a powerhouse for connectivity, no matter how far away devices are from a router. To prove it, we've done the testing to help you find the right mesh system.

At Tom's Guide, we put each mesh Wi-Fi system through real-world scenarios, from multi-story homes to outdoor use. This allows us to see how fast internet speeds are at multiple ranges, especially through objects and walls. So, if you've been struggling to get a strong Wi-Fi signal across your home, the mesh Wi-Fi systems we recommend will help you sort that problem out.

According to recent reports, for the best mesh Wi-Fi system you can buy today, we recommend the MSI Roami BE Pro for reliable speeds and long-distance coverage. This Wi-Fi 7 mesh system will take you far for its price, but there are more options we've tested for homes.

Recent findings suggest that soon, you'll see more of the next standard of mesh Wi-Fi systems arrive with Wi-Fi 8. We've already tested the first Wi-Fi 8 router, but there's no need to rush to get this yet, as there aren't any consumer devices that can take advantage of it. In the meantime, we have even more mesh systems worth considering!

For the latest wireless connectivity, or to cover your home on a budget, this guide will help you find the best mesh Wi-Fi system for your needs, with in-depth reviews and test results. Let's dive in.

In a recent development, why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

The MSI Roamii BE Pro isn't the fastest around, nor does it deliver the longest range, but it excels at speeds, distances and setup for half the price of other tri-band WiFi 7 routers. That's why it's the best mesh Wi-Fi system we recommend for most, especially if you're looking for an affordable way to upgrade to Wi-Fi 7.

Industry observers note that the Roamii BE Pro immediately stands out for its real-world speed across a whole house, reaching 1.885 Gbps at 15 feet and still delivering 66.3 Mbps at a distant 90 feet. That kind of consistent performance means you won’t be left hunting for a signal in the farthest room.

In our testing, the Roamii BE Pro also excelled at mid-range distances, recording 815.2 Mbps at 50 feet — a result that puts it squarely among the fastest mesh systems we’ve seen.

We found it outpaces the TP-Link Deco BE23 at close range (1.885 Gbps vs. 1.449 Gbps), but its real advantage is balancing those speeds with broader coverage, a feat some rivals like the Netgear Orbi 870 only match at longer distances. That makes the Roamii BE Pro a better pick for anyone who wants both fast speeds and reliable whole-home coverage, not just one or the other.

See our speed measurements tested at different distances.

Recent findings suggest that during two weeks of everyday use, the Roamii BE Pro kept up without breaking a sweat. That includes streaming 4K video, downloading large files, gaming and emailing.

Plus, wired device fans get a trio of 2.5 Gbps LAN ports and a USB 3.0 port. It's just a shame that this isn't available in single or three-packs, meaning you'd have to buy another two-pack if you're looking to add more nodes. At least it isn't too pricey!

Industry observers note that setup is a breeze: after scanning the QR code, entering a network name and updating the firmware, I had both nodes running in just 15 minutes. If you want the quickest path to reliable, top-tier Wi-Fi 7 speeds without fuss, the Roamii BE Pro is the system to beat.

Industry observers note that the TP-Link Deco BE23 indicates that high-speed, Wi-Fi 7 connectivity in a mesh system doesn't have to cost you a premium. For as low as $180, you can get a set of three powerful mesh networking devices that offer up far-reaching connectivity with some absolutely amazing speeds.

In a recent development, each of the BE23 units comes in a neat, discreet design that can be placed anywhere while hiding in plain sight, and you can set up a connection for the whole house easily with TP-Link’s Deco app. Plus, any of the units can be used as a host router. Once you're set up, you can take control of your connectivity and devices via the app, like integrating and controlling Tapo, Kasa, Philips Hue and Matter home automation devices.

Speed is the star of the show, especially for this mesh system's affordable price. In our testing, we saw highs of 1.449 Gbps at 15 feet, and still 150.1 Mbps as far away as 90 feet. Those numbers beat many routers we've tested, even though it understandably falls behind the likes of a tri-band system (like the TP-Link Deco BE63 with 1.821 Gbps at 15 feet away).

Recent findings suggest that with a maximum range of 115 feet for each unit, this mesh system will take you far (quite literally, connectivity-wise). Now that's an excellent balance between price and performance.

What you won't get here are more advanced features, like the 6 GHz band (just 2.4GHz and 5GHz here) or a super-wide 320 MHz data channel, and there's only a pair of 2.5 Gbps networking ports without a USB port, which makes wired connections limited.

According to recent reports, for an affordable way to keep your whole home connected with fantastic internet speeds, the price is right with the TP-Link Deco BE23. It may not be the fastest or the most advanced, but for value, it's hard to go wrong with this mesh setup.

The Netgear Orbi 870 is a powerful mesh Wi-Fi system that really excels at medium and long ranges, even outperforming its larger, more expensive older sibling.

It has been revealed that despite its more premium price, I really like the more cylindrical design with a cleaner overall look of the Orbi 870 and the rest of the firm’s Wi-Fi 7-powered mesh kits. While you’ll often see it in white at online retailers, you can actually get an all-black version too, but only on Netgear’s site.

The Orbi 870 is a very reliable and feature-packed mesh Wi-Fi system that’s ideal for futureproofing your home network thanks to its slew of multi-gig ports, including a 10 Gbps input. In his testing, Brian saw speeds of 1.82 Gbps at close range (15 feet).

In a recent development, however, it was the Orbi 870’s mid- and long-range performance that impressed him the most. For instance, at 50 and 75 feet, this mesh Wi-Fi system had download speeds of over 600 Mbps, beating both the entry-level Orbi 770 and even the Orbi 970 at the top of Netgear’s mesh lineup.

Recent findings suggest that even at a distance of 90 feet from Brian’s test laptop, it was at just over 100 Mbps, while the Orbi 970 and even TP-Link’s Deco BE85 were under 50 Mbps. At launch, a two-pack cost $1,000 (though you can often find it cheaper now), so the Orbi 870 is certainly an investment, just like the rest of the devices in Netgear’s Orbi line.

However, if you have a large home you want to fill with a strong Wi-Fi signal and a top-tier multi-gig internet proposal, it could definitely be worth it. Just keep in mind that you will need to set aside some extra cash if you want to secure your home network with it using Netgear’s Armor security package or want extended technical support, as only 90 days are included.

The Acer Predator Connect T7 is a mesh Wi-Fi system with a heavy focus on gamers. However, unlike my previous mesh router pick for gaming, the Asus ROG Rapture GT6, it’s a Wi-Fi 7-powered device with a much more subtle look.

Sources indicate that instead of RGB and lots of logos, the Predator Connect T7 features a taller, rectangular design in white or black, and at first glance, it looks quite similar to an Xbox Series X. There’s a splash of RGB lighting on the top, but this mesh kit has a sleeker and more restrained look that I think definitely works in its favor.

In a recent development, just like with the best gaming routers, the Predator Connect T7 has a low-latency design that uses Intel’s Killer Prioritization engine for peak gaming performance. It also comes with free built-in security software and makes full use of all of Wi-Fi 7’s best features.

In a recent development, during testing, Brian saw download speeds of 1.9 Gbps at close range (15 feet) with good mid-range performance. While the Predator Connect T7 has a multi-gig input port, its wired Ethernet ports are limited to gigabit speeds, so plugging in one of the best gaming laptops won’t give you a significant speed boost over connecting via Wi-Fi.

The Acer Predator Connect T7 is one of the few mesh Wi-Fi systems specifically designed for gamers and if you want a mesh router that looks as slick as your gaming PC, it’s a significant step up from the Asus ROG Rapture GT7 (which superseded the GT6 we used to recommend).

Industry observers note that however, it is on the expensive side at $330 per device, and unlike other mesh kits, you won’t see any discounts at all when buying a multi-pack. Still, if you want gaming-level network performance with the added benefits of mesh and want something less flashy, the Predator Connect T7 is an excellent mesh Wi-Fi system and the only one for gamers with Wi-Fi 7 support so far.

It has been revealed that the Eero Pro 7 is a smaller and sleeker mesh Wi-Fi system that’s incredibly simple to set up and use. Unlike Eero’s past mesh kits, which had a puck-shaped design, this one has a rounded rectangular shape and, at 7.1 x 5.8 x 2.6 inches, you won’t have any trouble finding a place for it and its satellites around your home.

After testing the larger, more powerful Eero Max 7 myself, I really like the Pro 7’s more compact design and the fact that it's significantly cheaper, too. The biggest selling point of the Pro 7 and Eero’s other mesh Wi-Fi systems is that even a home networking novice will have no trouble at all getting them up and running.

Industry observers note that setup and configuration are handled entirely through the very user-friendly Eero app. Besides how it looks, I really like the way that updates are downloaded and installed automatically, so your mesh Wi-Fi system is always running the latest software.

In his testing, Brian saw download speeds of 1.9 Gbps at close distances (15 feet), but the Pro 7 was equally impressive at mid-range distances with speeds just under a gigabit.

The Eero Pro 7 does cost a bit more than the competition, but nowhere close to what you’d pay for an Orbi mesh kit. As an Amazon manufacturer, Eero works great with your Alexa-powered and other smart home devices, and you can even use an Echo Dot as a mesh extender to add some extra range to your home network.

If you want a fast and capable Wi-Fi 7-powered mesh system that’s simple to set up and just works, the Eero Pro 7 is very easy to recommend, especially since it's a lot cheaper than the Max 7. The one downside is that you’re limited to just two Ethernet ports, but they are the faster 5 Gbps variety, which is great if you have a multi-gig internet strategy.

Recent findings suggest that the TP-Link Deco BE85 is a top-of-the-line mesh Wi-Fi system that was actually the first mesh router with Wi-Fi 7 support. It builds on the cylindrical design of the Deco XE75 with a more refined and polished look, but it packs in a ton of multi-gig and even a USB port.

Recent findings suggest that as someone who upgraded to fiber internet, I love how it has its own SFP+ port, which lets you plug your fiber line directly in at the back instead of into a separate ONT box first. Even if you’re still using one of the best cable modems, though, the Deco BE85 is a powerful mesh Wi-Fi system that won’t disappoint when it comes to performance.

One thing that’s really convenient about this mesh kit and TP-Link’s other Deco devices is that they’re all identical out of the box and you can use any of them as your main router. The company’s Deco app also makes setup and configuration very easy, and in my experience, it’s on par with Eero’s app in terms of usability.

15 feet (Toms Guide): TP-Link Deco BE85 scores 1.736.

50 feet (Toms Guide): TP-Link Deco BE85 scores 790.4.

75 feet (Toms Guide): TP-Link Deco BE85 scores 179.2.

90 feet (Toms Guide): TP-Link Deco BE85 scores 42.6.

Industry observers note that during testing, Brian saw download speeds of 1.73 Gbps at a close distance (15 feet) and good mid-range speeds, too. While this might seem a bit low for a premium mesh Wi-Fi system, Brian was one of the first people to get and review the Deco BE85. It's possible this has improved with firmware updates since its launch.

The Deco BE85 has come down in price since it released, but it’s still expensive, even though this model does go on sale quite frequently. However, if you have a fast, multi-gig fiber internet plan and want top-notch Wi-Fi 7 performance, this mesh router is the only one I’ve seen yet with an SFP+ port on the back.

It’s worth noting that, just like with Eero, all TP-Link Deco devices are compatible with one another, so you could always mix and match or upgrade to a more powerful model later on if you need to.

The mesh Wi-Fi systems we've used all come with amazing speeds, and we've done the testing to show how fast a router is at short and long ranges. But you'll find some will perform better at various distances, even if one delivers the fastest speeds around.

As an example, the Acer Predator Connect T7 offers the fastest speeds at 15 feet, but it loses out to the likes of the TP-Link Deco BE23 and others at 90 feet. It comes down to what you prioritize: speed or range (or a balance of both!).

So, to compare each mesh Wi-Fi system across the range of distances we've tested, check out the versus table below to help you make the right choice for your home.

Select a mesh Wi-Fi system to compare internet speed at different distances (measured in Gbps and Mbps).

Sources indicate that we test every mesh Wi-Fi system to measure performance and range, using Keysight IxChariot. Testing is done in a multi-story home with brick walls. When we test standard routers, we look at performance at a distance to provide real-world information about coverage and speeds. In addition to lab testing, we evaluate the ease of setup and features of each device, too.

Industry observers note that we measure performance at a 15-foot distance without obstructions, so that we can gauge the maximum amount of data that a router can move. Higher throughput will serve you better in data-heavy uses, like streaming video, gaming, or connecting multiple customers at once.

It has been revealed that range measures the furthest usable distance for a particular router. Longer ranges are better for larger homes, where rooms are spread out at a distance. We measure how much data a router can move at 15, 50, 75 and 90 feet, as well as the maximum coverage area of a mesh Wi-Fi system.

It has been revealed that we also test how well each mesh Wi-Fi system transmits and receives signals through drywall, brick, concrete and even metal walls, and how each handles coverage in a two- or three-story home. They also go through additional testing to see how well each system does when sending a signal through the main router and through the included satellites.

Of course (and most importantly), we also consider what you really get for your money, considering which features are worthwhile and how any given product compares with other devices from competing manufacturers.

A lot of factors come into choosing the mesh Wi-Fi system that will suit your space, from the coverage you need to the speeds you demand — all for the right price. We've got just the tips to make your choice easier.

Recent findings suggest that wi-Fi 8 is currently still in the early stages of being supported on all devices, so you won't be able to take advantage of the new connectivity standard right now. Currently, no consumer devices support Wi-Fi 8 coverage, and we're not expecting to see support until sometime in 2027 or 2028.

We've reviewed the first Wi-Fi 8 router, the Asus ROG Rapture GT-BN98 Pro, and are impressed by its incredible Wi-Fi speeds and range. However, we couldn't see its full potential since we're still waiting for Wi-Fi 8 hardware. We'll have to see how well mesh Wi-Fi systems with Wi-Fi 8 perform, too.

Recent findings suggest that while Wi-Fi 8 isn't worth getting right now, it may be worth it to many looking to future-proof their homes once more devices adopt Wi-Fi 8. Besides, it's backwards compatible with Wi-Fi 7, Wi-Fi 6 and so on. We'll keep you updated in the meantime.

According to recent reports, yes, a mesh Wi-Fi system can go through walls. Because Wi-Fi uses radio waves, these waves can pass through solid materials like walls to connect to a device.

However, when Wi-Fi meets a wall, some of it goes through, some bounces off and some is absorbed. Because of this, the signal can be weaker, especially when more walls are in the way.

A mesh Wi-Fi system has an advantage in getting past this. Instead of using one router to get a signal, a mesh system uses multiple nodes placed throughout a home to bypass hard objects or walls in order to get an unobstructed signal. This means there are fewer barriers to getting a clear Wi-Fi signal.

Industry observers note that the main downside of using a mesh Wi-Fi system is that it can be very expensive, especially compared to traditional Wi-Fi routers. These are only needed for those living in large homes or for anyone who needs Wi-Fi coverage over a long distance. For those in smaller spaces, this is overkill.

Since mesh systems come in a multi-pack of nodes, this bumps up the price, as these extra devices deliver a better range of coverage throughout a space compared to other routers.

Sources indicate that nodes also must be placed close enough to catch a strong signal, which can be tricky in a home with many rooms separated by concrete or brick walls. Plus, with this signal hopping between multiple nodes, there may be an increase in latency, which isn't ideal for competitive gameplay.

Otherwise, the best mesh Wi-Fi systems try to overcome these downsides, and these are still the best option to upgrade your home network wirelessly.

Mesh Wi-Fi systems come with nodes and are usually available in two-packs or three-packs, but deciding which one to get depends on the size of your home. If you live in a small or medium house, then a two-pack will usually do the trick. For large homes with more than three bedrooms or multiple stories, a three-pack is the better choice, as this will ensure that your Wi-Fi signal reaches every corner and even upstairs.

In a recent development, the great thing about mesh Wi-Fi systems, though, is that you can always start small and work up to something bigger. For instance, if you buy a two-pack and find that you’re still dealing with Wi-Fi dead zones in certain parts of your home, you can always add another node later to improve your coverage.

In a recent development, plug-in Wi-Fi extenders aren’t nearly as advanced or as powerful as the nodes in a mesh Wi-Fi system. The other substantial problem with Wi-Fi extenders is that most of them create a separate network you have to manually switch to each time you want to use them. For instance, let’s say you put a Wi-Fi extender in your bedroom. Whenever you want to get online in that particular room, you’ll have to switch from your main Wi-Fi network to the extender, which gets annoying really fast.

In a recent development, on the other hand, with a mesh Wi-Fi system, the nodes are all part of your main network and no switching is required. As you move from one side of your house to the other, your mesh system automatically hands off your connection to whatever satellite you’re closest to, which ensures you have a strong signal and a good connection wherever you are in your home.

Recent findings suggest that as someone who's been working from home for the past eight years, Anthony Spadafora has tried everything from Wi-Fi extenders to powerline adapters to get the most out of his home network, before finally upgrading to a mesh Wi-Fi system. Along the way, he's tested out loads of different routers and network configurations. Based on what he's learned, Anthony tries to highlight the critical role Wi-Fi routers play in our day-to-day lives and how a mesh network can help solve the most common connectivity issues like Wi-Fi dead spots.

With experience in testing, using and evaluating wireless data from before Wi-Fi was even a word, Brian Nadel has tried out and reviewed every major router available in his home networking lab. A LAN nerd, his philosophy is to use the router the way you would, testing networking gear for ease of setup, performance, security and above all for value. The result is peace of mind when it comes to choosing the right router.

iOS 27 basically turns your iPhone and AirPods into an Apple Watch at the gym

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (877 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that gymKit has been one of Apple Watch’s smartest fitness features since it released in 2017.
  • It has been revealed that with iOS 27, Apple is expanding that idea beyond Apple Watch.
  • I tapped my iPhone to the treadmill, picked Indoor Walk (Indoor Run is also offered), and started the workout from the treadmill.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that gymKit has been one of Apple Watch’s smartest fitness features since it released in 2017. Tap your watch to compatible gym equipment, and Apple Watch shares your heart rate while the machine sends back metrics like distance, incline, pace, and calories.

It has been revealed that with iOS 27, Apple is expanding that idea beyond Apple Watch. I tested the latest GymKit on iPhone and AirPods Pro 3 ($149, reg. $249) experience with a GymKit-compatible treadmill. It basically gives you the Apple Watch GymKit workout tracking experience, just without the watch. This could be useful in a lot of scenarios.

The setup is simple. I tapped my iPhone to the treadmill, picked Indoor Walk (Indoor Run is also offered), and started the workout from the treadmill. With GymKit, workout data is stored privately on iPhone and removed from the equipment.

It has been revealed that once the workout started, the treadmill received heart-rate data from AirPods Pro 3. Meanwhile, the Fitness app on iPhone received the treadmill’s distance, pace, incline, and calorie data. Treadmills know details that an iPhone and AirPods can’t know on their own, especially incline and precise belt distance.

As a side note: Apple Watch has more accurate treadmill workout tracking as part of watchOS 27. GymKit remains the gold standard for accurate data, though.

GymKit also avoids two awkward gym habits. You don’t need to hold the treadmill’s metal heart-rate contacts while jogging. You also do not need to wear a Bluetooth heart-rate strap.

AirPods Pro 3 become the heart-rate source (and likely your podcast or music audio source as well). iPhone becomes the workout computer, which you can monitor during your workout. And the treadmill fills in the machine data while providing the surface for walking or running.

Apple has been moving more fitness features onto iPhone for years. iOS first made the Fitness app useful without Apple Watch as Apple Fitness+ leaned into iPhone as an entry point. AirPods Pro 3 pushed that further as the first AirPods with heart-rate tracking, after Apple tested the idea with Powerbeats Pro 2.

iOS 27 brings those pieces together. GymKit on iPhone shouldn’t replace Apple Watch for people who wear one every day. Instead, it’s a great backup when your Apple Watch is dead, charging, or left at home.

It also gives iPhone and AirPods users a taste of the Apple Watch experience, which could attract future Apple Watch customers.

Sources indicate that in testing with iOS 27 beta 1, my Exercise ring didn’t enhancement as I worked out without wearing Apple Watch. But after I put my watch back on, the Exercise ring caught up, and the workout appeared in Fitness with the right data.

My sample 16-minute treadmill walk demonstrated 0.66 miles, 65 active calories, 97 total calories, 32 feet of elevation gain, and a 115 BPM average heart rate, just like if I’d worn an Apple Watch.

I had been getting the impression that gym equipment manufacturers had been abandoning GymKit support - if they ever had done so initially. I even got the impression that the majority of equipment in Apple's own onsite Gym at the Apple Park may not have supported it - at least originally.

It has been revealed that does Apple have a webpage listing compatible brands and models? Like they do/did for HomeKit.

What is other people perception? Any rowing machines that support it?

…checks - surprisingly it looks like Peloton do support it on their bikes.

If I tried to use GymKit on iPhone without AirPods, the iPhone disconnected when the workout started because it had no heart-rate source. If I tried to start GymKit from iPhone while wearing Apple Watch, iOS pointed me back to the Workout app on Apple Watch instead, though you can continue without using the watch.

It has been revealed that airPods heart-rate permission also matters. You can manage it in Settings under your AirPods settings and privacy options. I had turned it off, mostly as a theoretical battery-saving move, but this test convinced me to turn it back on. AirPods Pro 3 can also work with Apple Watch to provide the best available heart-rate data.

Industry observers note that gymKit on iPhone is one of those iOS 27 features that sounds small until it solves a real problem. If Apple Watch is your default workout tracker, it probably stays that way.

But if your watch dies or you forget it at home, iPhone plus AirPods Pro 3 can now log a treadmill workout with real heart-rate data and real treadmill metrics.

Arsenal suffered back-to-back pre-season defeats as they lost 3-2 to Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup on Sunday.

The loss to the German side followed a 3-1 defeat by Real Betis on Wednesday night in Dublin.

Before kick-off, Bruno Guimarães was paraded to the Arsenal faithful after completing his £75m move from Newcastle on Saturday.

Sources indicate that but enthusiasm about the Brazilian’s arrival was dampened when Dortmund took the lead at the Emirates inside the opening 10 minutes. Felix Nmecha’s incisive pass into the penalty area was met by the run of Samuele Inácio, who made no mistake with a clinical finish into the far corner.

According to recent reports, ten minutes after half-time, Arsenal pulled a goal back through Ethan Nwaneri, who scored from Christos Tzolis’s cross. However, moments later Dortmund restored their two-goal advantage as Joane Gadou smashed home from a corner.

Arsenal kept their hopes alive through a Viktor Gyokeres penalty after Tzolis was brought down, but Dortmund were able to hold on to claim victory. After the full-time whistle, there was a penalty shoot-out, which Arsenal won 5-4.

In a recent development, arsenal still have a number of players to return to action following their World Cup exploits, including Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke. As well as Guimarães, there was another addition on display at the Emirates: Arsenal have added last year’s title win to the list of honours displayed inside the stadium.

According to recent reports, tzolis takes the free-kick and delivers it to the far post, where Gabriel meets it but his powerful header goes over the bar. The Brazilian probably should have scored.

Mikel Arteta has made a change as Nwaneri has replaced Odegaard, who has only recently returned to training after the World Cup.

According to recent reports, with it being a warm day in north London, we have a water break. Hopefully they do not catch on after the World Cup. Mikel Arteta is looking pretty animated talking to his side.

What a finish that is to put the German side 2-0 up! 18-year-old Karetsas, who has joined Dortmund from Genk this summer, is afforded too much space outside the Arsenal penalty area as he drives towards the box and punishes the hosts for that, curling a sublime shot into the far corner.

Recent findings suggest that odegaard slides a clever pass into the right channel to pick out the run of Gyokeres towards the Dortmund box. Mane though slides in with a perfectly-timed challenge to take it off Gyokeres. Mane had to time that right with the challenge being right on the edge of his own box.

It has been revealed that arsenal hit the bar. Dowman does well down Arsenal’s right to drive into the Dortmund box and cuts it back to Gyokeres. The Swedish striker takes a few touches before getting his shot away, which clips the top of the bar.

A dangerous cross from the left comes all the way to Svensson at the back post but he lacked conviction with his header and it goes wide. Perhaps he should be hitting the target.

Down at the other end Arsenal have a headed chance of their own. Havertz clips in a cross from the left and picks out Gyokeres. The Swede is a fair way out from goal and his header goes wide.

Should Havertz have done better with this opportunity? The German is played in down the right channel and has Gyokeres calling for the cross in space in the centre of the box. Havertz tries to find him but Meyer is out to smother it. Had Havertz found Gyokeres, it would likely have been a simple tap-in for the Swede.

Odegaard appears to be through one-on-one but then goes down just outside the Dortmund box. Mane pleads his innocence but referee Chris Kavanagh does not agree, giving a free-kick. If this was a competitive game, Mane would potentially have been sent off.

Gyokeres will take and opts for power over accuracy. It is safe to say his effort is terrible, blazing over the bar and missing the target by some margin.

Calafiori trips Bellingham as Dortmund attempted to counter. If this was a competitive fixture, Calafiori likely would have been booked for that foul.

Bellingham and Havertz are involved in quite the collision. Both players go for the header and Havertz just gets to it first. Havertz is awarded the foul and is ok.

Industry observers note that the German side take the lead inside the opening seven minutes. Nmecha slides a lovely pass through the Arsenal defensive line to pick out the run of Inacio into the Arsenal penalty area. It is a clinical finish from Inacio, who slides his effort into the far corner,.

According to recent reports, dortmund’s first proper foray forward causes Arsenal issues and Tzolis is forced to put it behind for Dortmund’s first corner of the game. The inswinger though to the front post is poor and Gyokeres easily heads away from danger.

Gyokeres wins Arsenal their first corner of the game out on the right. Odegaard’s delivery into the near post causes problems for Dortmund and forces Dortmund keeper Meyer to tip over his own bar for another Arsenal corner. Meyer this time punches Odegaard’s delivery away and Dortmund clear their lines.

We are under way at the Emirates.

Moments after Bruno Guimaraes’ unveiling, both sides now emerge from the tunnel and we are moments away from kick-off at the Emirates.

It has been revealed that just before the two sides emerge the tunnel, there is a special guest who comes out first in the form of Bruno Guimaraes. Chants of “Bruno! Bruno!” ring around the Emirates as the Arsenal fans get their first glimpse of him in an Arsenal shirt, although the Brazilian is not involved today.

Reports are that Jobe’s older brother Jude is at the Emirates today, not that Arsenal fans should think that Jude is swapping Real Madrid for the red half of north London.

Recent findings suggest that arsenal took the Premier League trophy with them to Dublin on Wednesday night and it is on show today at the Emirates. They kick off the defence of their crown on opening night against newly-promoted Coventry is just under two weeks.

Counting down until kick-off ⏰ Make sure you're in your seats by 1.45pm (UK), Gooners - we have a very special guest in store 👀.

According to recent reports, when Bruno Guimarães signed for Newcastle United from Lyon in January 2022, much was made of the idea that he had rejected Arsenal in favour of a move to St James’ Park. The Brazilian played along with it, posting a video on his social media pages which featured multiple newspaper headlines about Arsenal wanting to buy him.

Sources indicate that the Newcastle fans, still delirious about the recent takeover by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, understandably lapped it up. Their dream was to overthrow the established powers in English football, and the capture of Guimarães was regarded as a sign that they were truly ready to challenge teams of Arsenal’s stature and wealth.

Even the lyrics to the midfielder’s chant referred to the north Londoners, as Newcastle fans sang that Guimarães “could have signed for Arsenal” but chose instead to play “in the famous black and white”.

Yesterday Arsenal confirmed the signing of Brazilian midfielder Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle for £75m on a four-year deal, with the option of a further year. Here is what the Brazilian had to say:.

Recent findings suggest that “I feel good, I feel amazing. I am glad for the opportunity. Since the first time I spoke to (Andrea) Berta and Mikel (Arteta) I was excited. I just felt inside of me that I need a fresh challenge in my life and I think to be an Arsenal player is going to be an exciting challenge in my life.

Recent findings suggest that “I think after playing two World Cups, I am at the point of my life, I think I need a challenge like this. I want to win trophies, I want to make history and I think I am in the right place to do it. I am so excited to start. We have tough games to play this season so the squad is going to be very, very crucial and I am hopeful we can achieve our dreams.”.

According to recent reports, premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the latest season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

It has been revealed that “I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

It has been revealed that “I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”.

This is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace. After today, Arsenal have two more games, including the Community Shield in a week’s time, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

It has been revealed that dortmund, led by Niko Kovac, finished second in the Bundesliga last season, 16 points off winners Bayern Munich. They have played four pre-season friendlies thus far, winning twice and losing twice. The likes of Karim Adeyemi, Julian Brandt and Niklas Sule have left the club this summer.

#85358. Cloudflare hides shortcomings of the underlying infrastructure

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (408 w)

Cloudflare hides shortcomings of the underlying infrastructure

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (408 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Charlie

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, cloudflare has arguably done more to push modern internet technologies than any other organization.
  • While this is great, Cloudflare also hides many of the shortcomings of the underlying infrastructure from both users and website owners.
  • It has been revealed that one of my biggest problems with this is the fact that Cloudflare doesn't do enough to notify website administrators about these concerns.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, cloudflare has arguably done more to push modern internet technologies than any other organization. The work they have done to enable TLS, IPv6, post quantum encryption, and other modern standards for millions of websites deserves a tremendous amount of credit.

While this is great, Cloudflare also hides many of the shortcomings of the underlying infrastructure from both users and website owners. Yes, you can connect to a Cloudflare website and it'll allow for IPv6, post quantum encryption, and TLS. But Cloudflare's connection to the origin server might be entirely unencrypted and rely exclusively on IPv4. This creates a huge mismatch between what is being presented to users and the reality of the connection.

It has been revealed that one of my biggest problems with this is the fact that Cloudflare doesn't do enough to notify website administrators about these concerns. While Cloudflare provides tools to inspect these, comprehensive visibility is lacking. The Cloudflare dashboard should notify you about each of these issues where Cloudflare is following better practices than your origin server, without website administrators having to dig through and specifically look for this information. Clear warnings and proactive alerts to administrators would help greatly.

Not only that, but according to Cloudflare's own documentation, they actively prefer IPv4 over IPv6 when making origin server requests, which is particularly disappointing for a company that has done so much to advance IPv6 adoption:.

For proxied DNS records that have both an IPv6 and IPv4 origin address, Cloudflare will prefer the IPv4 address when connecting to your origin server.

Even when website administrators invest in deploying IPv6 on their origin servers, Cloudflare still prioritizes IPv4.

It has been revealed that I also believe the industry should consider adding functionality so CDNs and other intermediate networks can expose origin TLS connection information alongside their own. This would allow users and network researchers to better understand the encryption state of the entire path and hold website owners accountable for bad security practices. A similar mechanism could expose which IP version is being used to communicate with the origin server.

Cloudflare has an opportunity to not only make modern internet technologies accessible to consumers, but also encourage adoption of those technologies throughout the underlying infrastructure. Cloudflare should be a catalyst for modernizing the internet, not a mechanism that allows website owners to avoid modernization indefinitely. Improving transparency would be a meaningful step toward achieving that goal.
